title: See the dots
prompt:
Time to see the data on your own screen. Run `plot_tickets.py` inside your virtual environment. A window opens with a scatter plot of hours against cost for the twelve fictional tickets. Close the window to end the program.

Then try the second picture: change `ax.scatter(hours, costs)` to `ax.hist(costs)` and run it again.

Last, keep a copy: add `fig.savefig("tickets.png")` on the line before `plt.show()`, run it once more, and look for `tickets.png` in your folder.
hints: No window? Check that the virtual environment is active (`source .venv/bin/activate`) and that Matplotlib installed without errors.
The program waits while the window is open. Close the window and the terminal prompt comes back.
`ax.hist` needs only one list, the costs. `ax.scatter` needs two, one for across and one for up.
explain_after: That is Matplotlib's basic pattern: `plt.subplots()` makes a figure with one Axes, a method draws on the Axes, and `plt.show()` displays it [ml-020]. `scatter` and `hist` are both Axes methods [ml-102]. Look for the dot far up and to the right: the fridge job. Spotting a lonely dot like that before you build a model is the whole point of this level. `savefig` saved the figure to a file, and the `.png` ending picked the format [ml-112].
